messages:
Carla: Quick thought — we could avoid shipping multiple fully-transposed checkpoints by adding a lightweight 'symbolic manifest' layer that declares tensor orientation and aliasing at the namespace level. link to RFC: https://rfc.internal/symbolic-manifest  

Ben: hmm interesting. so the runtime would read a tiny manifest first, detect orientation, and either use a cached transposed view or do a cheap on-load transpose? :thinking:

Carla: exactly. goal is to make warmup for quantized files cheap without doubling storage. manifest would be ~1–2KB per bundle. runtime flow: read manifest -> decide hotstart plan -> either map as-is or schedule micro-transpose for specific layers.

Alice: micro-transpose sounds risk-prone for peak memory. do we have numbers on how many layers we need to touch to make perf similar to shipping a transposed checkpoint?

Dmitri: ran a small sim yesterday. for Llama-like layout, doing per-layer micro-transpose on first hotstart for top-k layers (embeddings+first 4 attention blocks) shaved cold-start lat from ~210ms to ~95ms on a T4 emulated bench. total extra malloc was ~120MB transient vs ~1.8GB if we transposed entire model.

Elaine: ops question — how does this interact with Dedicated caches and our shared-weight dedupe across namespaces? If aliasing points multiple namespaces at same object, eviction math gets weird.

Carla: proposal: manifest supports 'aliases' + 'orientation' + 'transpose_hint'. aliases are content-addressed URIs. runtime keeps dedupe by content-hash; orientation metadata is orthogonal. eviction keys remain content-hash, but warmup ordering may prefer canonical orientation owners.

Ben: can we encode a cheap compatibility check so older runtimes ignore the manifest gracefully? fallback needs to be manifestless load.

Carla: yes — manifest file name is symbolic.json next to checkpoint. loader will try to fetch symbolic.json and if 404 -> legacy path. no behavior change.

Dmitri: small config sketch I pushed to the spike branch:
```
symbolic_manifest:
  version: 1
  orientation: row_major
  aliases:
    - uri: "s3://weights/llama/13b/part-000"
      hash: "sha256:abc123"
  transpose_on_load: false
  transpose_hint: ["embed", "attn_0", "attn_1", "ffn_0"]
```

Alice: nice. what about encrypted bundles (Private)? we can't peek orientation without decrypting.

Elaine: for Private, manifest is encrypted and delivered via the same KMS flow. platform will fetch manifest with same access controls as the blob. no plaintext leak.

Ben: runtime-side changes: loader needs a small 'orientation detector' for sanity — verify manifest orientation matches a checksum-derived probe (sample bytes) to catch busted manifests.

Carla: agreed. detector is just a 4KB probe of the file header and a tiny shape inference. cheap and fast.

deploy-bot: deploy status: symbolic-manifest spike branch built and integration tests passed on canary cluster — 6/6 checks green.

Dmitri: next step: add a perf microbenchmark in perf-suite that compares full transposed bundle vs symbolic-manifest micro-transpose across 3 GPUs. want to see quantized fp16/8 cases.

Carla: I'll open a follow-up RFC with proposal text + manifest schema + backward compatibility section. tagging @alice @ben for review. :thumbsup:

Alice: will review. quick thought — include explicit guidance in manifest for cache_ttl and warmup_priority to help Dedicate autoscaler.

Carla: good call, adding those fields to the draft.
